policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the singular 'his son', matching the qere בֶן; the ketiv בני is plural ('his sons'), which the English does not reflect. The 'other'-class note ('According to another reading, son') is not a mapped textual_variant note and does not decide the unit; the wording alone does.

ASV 'that he might not reign in Jerusalem' renders the qere מִמְּלֹךְ (min + infinitive, 'from reigning'); the ketiv במלך ('when he reigned') is the reading the 'other'-class note relegates to the margin. The wording decides; the alternative_rendering note ('Or, fine') concerns 'tribute' and is irrelevant.
ASV transliterates the mother's name as 'Zebidah', which reflects the ketiv זבידה (yod after the beth); the qere זְבוּדָּה would yield 'Zebuddah'. The ASV wording follows the ketiv here.
